notes: Two scenario families. (A) Skeleton evals 1-4 scope activation + config-derived tier derivation only; they do not exercise a specific mode body. Their prompts are generic ('steward this project') with no explicit mode signal, so the front door completes pre-flight, derives tiers, then stops and asks which of the four modes to run (per references/mode-routing.md Stop and ask) — it does not guess a mode. The fallback scenario stops earlier, at tier derivation, before routing is reached. (B) Routing evals 5-8 (setup_scenario 'routing') provide REQ-01 verification for issue 6c5f70ad: each carries one of the four representative opening requests from references/mode-routing.md and checks the front door classifies it into the CORRECT mode (1/2/3/4) and begins that mode's handoff, HALTING at the handoff boundary — it does not run the full mode body (no execution leads dispatched, no planning interview, no sweep). The 'routing' setup seeds the this-repo two-tier ruleset plus one existing anchor-tier (type:milestone) container 'Demo release readiness' with two epic children; setup-test-repo.sh prints MILESTONE_ID=<short_id> on its last line, which substitutes into the mode-1 prompt's {CONTAINER_ID} placeholder (modes 2/3/4 ignore the container). Each eval requires a fresh test repo created by setup-test-repo.sh, which the sub-agent must be pointed at (cwd = that repo). The jit binary is at /home/vkaskivuo/.cargo/bin/jit. The skill files are at /home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/; the skill reads the canonical content standards from the jit repo through the ~/.claude/skills symlink, so the test repo need not carry it. MCP disabled to avoid contaminating production .jit. Expected tier outputs are grounded in the derivation contract (references/tier-derivation.md worked verification): steward anchor = first strategic_types entry; delegation boundary = union of applies_to across templates.

evals.name: activation-and-preflight
evals.prompt: You are a project steward. Your working directory is a test project at {REPO_PATH}. The jit binary is at /home/vkaskivuo/.cargo/bin/jit. Read the jit-project-lead skill at /home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/SKILL.md and follow it to steward this project. Run the skill exactly as written and report what it does. In your final report, state each pre-flight step you performed and its result, the tier-derivation outputs, and where and why the skill stopped.
evals.expected_output: The jit-project-lead skill activates and executes its pre-flight in order: confirms .jit/ exists, runs `jit recover`, reads .jit/config.toml (type hierarchy and strategic_types), reads .jit/templates.toml (the applies_to lists), and reads the canonical content-standards doc. It then performs tier derivation once and, reaching mode dispatch with a generic prompt that carries no explicit mode signal, stops and asks which of the four modes to run rather than guessing one, without authoring any mode behavior. No .jit/ issue state is created or mutated (only `jit recover`'s lock cleanup is permitted).

evals.expected_output: With .jit/templates.toml absent, tier derivation routes to the numeric-level fallback rather than the primary path. The run reads the level map from `jit config show-hierarchy --json`, recovers a candidate proposal (anchor = milestone from strategic_types; boundary = {epic}, the type at the next distinct level below the anchor), and then STOPS and asks the invoker to confirm, explicitly naming .jit/templates.toml as the missing input and reporting what show-hierarchy returned. It does NOT apply the recovered tiers unconfirmed and does not proceed past derivation: no .jit/ issue state is created or mutated and the config/templates are left as-is.

The opening request is: "Drive milestone {CONTAINER_ID} to done — steward it across its epics." Run the skill's pre-flight, tier derivation, and mode-routing front door. CLASSIFY this opening request into exactly one of the four invocation modes, then begin only that mode's handoff and HALT at the handoff boundary: do NOT run the full mode body (do not dispatch any execution lead, do not run a planning interview, do not run a standards sweep). In your final report, state the derived tiers, which mode number (1/2/3/4) you routed to and why, and — for the mode you picked — the handoff you began (for mode 1: the container you resolved by id, its type, and whether it is the anchor tier). Report only the bounded routing decision.
evals.expected_output: The skill completes pre-flight and tier derivation (anchor = milestone, boundary = {epic}, two tier), then classifies the opening request as MODE 1 (lead an already-existing strategic container): the request names an id that resolves to one existing anchor-tier container. It begins mode 1's resolve-and-handoff: resolves the seed container by id via `jit issue show`, confirms its type equals the ANCHOR TYPE (milestone) so it is at the steward anchor tier, and hands it to `## Sub-strategic dispatch` — naming the resolved container. It HALTS at that handoff boundary: it does NOT enter the dispatch loop, does NOT dispatch any jit-execution-lead, and does not run waves or coherence review. It routes to mode 1 only, with no misroute to modes 2/3/4. No .jit/ issue state is created or mutated (only `jit recover`'s lock cleanup is permitted).
